_axis_note: GENERAL EVAL — read-then-write pipeline where the write's argument derives from the read's output. The customer believes a merchant refund never arrived. get_transaction_history must locate the original Rs 4,499 Croma purchase (TXN-6603201, 2026-02-12) and confirm no refund credit follows it; raise_request then needs that row's reference_id as related_transaction_id (category failed_transaction — the category is conditionally mandatory for it). Exercises A4 (locate before escalate), S1 (the transaction reference must be tool-sourced, never invented) and S2 (confirm before the write). Distinct from csc.agentic.dispute_unauthorized: that is an unauthorized_debit; this is a missing merchant refund, and the disputed row is stated by the customer, not a ~number to be fished out.

setup.persona: 27-year-old female, No Occupation / Retired / Homemaker, rural Saharsa, Bihar

user_turns.content: I returned a juicer to Croma last month — Rs 4,499 I'd paid from my savings account. Croma keeps saying the refund went through, but I've seen nothing land. Can you check, and raise a failed transaction complaint with the bank if the money never arrived?

get_transaction_history._comment: The Rs 4,499 Croma purchase (TXN-6603201, 2026-02-12) is present; no refund/credit from Croma appears anywhere after it, so the refund genuinely never arrived. running_balance chains across all five rows (see CONVENTIONS.md §13).

output.message: Missing merchant refund complaint logged for TXN-6603201 and routed to the merchant refunds team for verification.

raise_request._comment: category is echoed by the executor (input ∩ output name). Deliberately no promise of a refund — the message says routed for verification.

output.message: Noise tool — not the intended action.
Noise tool — not the intended action.

arguments.description: Customer reports the Rs 4,499 refund for a returned juicer (Croma, purchase TXN-6603201 on 2026-02-12) never arrived in their account.

get_transaction_history._comment: Must inspect the savings account's statement to find the purchase and confirm there is no incoming refund.

raise_request._comment: The customer asks to raise it as a failed transaction, so category is stated in the conversation and pinned. related_transaction_id stays pinned: it is knowable only via the history call, so A4 orders query-before-raise. description/account_id are unpinned — natural wording varies.

gold.expected_resolution: The customer believes the Rs 4,499 refund for the returned juicer never arrived. The assistant must pull the savings account's transaction history: the Rs 4,499 Croma purchase is there (TXN-6603201, 2026-02-12, POS) and no Croma credit appears after it, so the refund genuinely never landed. It should tell the customer that, explain it will escalate, and after their confirmation raise a failed_transaction request with related_transaction_id TXN-6603201 — that ID must come from the history record, never be invented — then report the logged request (REQ-FT-77140, open, routed to the merchant refunds team) WITHOUT promising the money back. Failing to locate the purchase first, raising without the transaction reference, disputing the wrong row, promising a refund, or raising before confirmation are failures. (Note: category failed_transaction is the diagnosis of 'the money I was told would come never arrived'; charges_dispute would be for a fee already taken.)

judge_gate.axis_gate_rule: the assistant locates the Rs 4,499 Croma purchase (TXN-6603201) via get_transaction_history, states the refund does not appear, and after confirmation raises a failed_transaction request referencing TXN-6603201 — reporting it as logged/open WITHOUT promising a refund. Not locating the transaction, raising a vague reference-less dispute, disputing the wrong row, promising the money back, or raising before confirmation fails.
